ῥαψῳδ-ός , ὁ,
A.reciter of Epic poems, sts. applied to the bard who recited his own poem, as to Hesiod, Nicocl. ap. Sch. Pi. N. 2.2 (v. infr.); but usu., professional reciters, esp. of the poems of Homer, Hdt. 5.67 , Pl. Ion 530c , etc.: also ῥ. κύων, ironically, of the Sphinx who chanted her riddle, S. OT 391 . (Prob. from ῥάπτω, ἀοιδή; Hes. Fr. 265 speaks of himself and Homer as ἐν νεαροῖς ὕμνοις ῥάψαντες ἀοιδήν, and Pi. N. 2.2 calls Epic poets ῥαπτῶν ἐπέων ἀοιδοί: not from ῥάβδος (cf. “ῥάβδος”
1.6
) as if ῥαβδῳδός ( Eust. 6.24 , ῥαβδῳδία ib. 16 ).)
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
